assertions.notes: The answer opens by saying the defer is wrong, should be deleted, and should not be shipped as written.
It explains that RestoreTerminal pairs with ReleaseTerminal for temporary handoffs and turns Bubble Tea's terminal modes back on rather than returning the terminal to the shell.
It states that Run() restores the terminal after a normal quit, an error, or a recovered panic, and that panics are caught by default unless WithoutCatchPanics is set.
It tells the user to let Run() own cleanup and limits a custom cleanup boundary to the case where built-in recovery is disabled with WithoutCatchPanics.
The answer opens by saying not to ship the defer and gives a replacement pattern without it.
It describes RestoreTerminal as the other half of ReleaseTerminal, a handoff API that turns Bubble Tea's terminal modes back on rather than restoring the shell.
It says Run() restores the terminal on normal quit, on error, and on a recovered panic, and that panic recovery is on by default.
It warns against competing cleanup on the managed path and limits custom outer cleanup to cases that bypass Bubble Tea or use WithoutCatchPanics.
The answer opens with 'Don't ship this. Remove the defer,' saying it makes the panic case worse.
It explains RestoreTerminal is the partner of ReleaseTerminal and re-enables Bubble Tea's raw and screen modes rather than restoring the shell.
It states Program.Run() restores the terminal on normal quit, on error, and on a recovered panic in Init/Update/View/Cmd.
It tells the user no custom guard is needed and limits custom cleanup to the tea.WithoutCatchPanics() case; the goroutine recover is for error reporting, not terminal cleanup.
Identifies the double outer frame plus pane borders as nested borders and recommends deleting the outer frame, recovering 2 columns and 2 rows.
Counts readiness encoded three times (word, green, checkmark) and says a marker on nearly every row tells the reader nothing, so only exceptions should be marked.
Cuts the footer to 5–7 hints that change with the focused pane, ending in `? help`, and moves all 18 into a grouped help screen.
Puts responsive behavior first with concrete layouts for 80–119 columns, 60–79 columns, and an app-specific minimum of 50x12 shown as a too-small message.
At 60–79 columns it switches to a resources-only single pane where Enter opens the YAML full-screen, which is a drill-down rather than three shrunken columns.
The clutter table flags two levels of border nesting and says to delete the double outer frame because the terminal edge already frames the app.
It counts four ready signals (bullet, [READY], green, ✓) and says the bullet on 100% of rows marks nothing.
It replaces the 18-key footer with one row of 3–5 focus-aware hints ending in `?`, plus a full `?` help screen grouped by pane.
It makes responsive behavior the top blocker and gives concrete layouts for 80×24 (80–119 band), 60–79 columns, and a too-small screen below 50×12.
At 60–79 columns it switches to one pane at a time with Enter/Esc drill-down, and it says panes should disappear at set widths rather than keep shrinking.
Measures border-nesting depth as 2 and recommends deleting the double-line outer frame, noting it recovers 2 rows and 2 columns.
Counts four readiness signals (bullet, [READY], green, ✓) and states that a marker on every row marks nothing, so only exceptions should be marked.
Cuts the footer to 4–6 contextual hints generated from the keymap, ending with `? help`, and moves the full list to a `?` overlay plus a `:` command mode.

Treats responsiveness as the top priority and gives a width ladder: the 80–119 range collapses namespaces into the header, 60–79 becomes a single drill-down pane, and below 48×12 shows a too-small message.
Specifies a single-pane drill-down (namespace → resources → YAML, Esc to go back) at 60–79 columns and warns that squeezing three panes is unusable.
Opens with 'don't make it a full-screen app', recommends inline with a height cap of about 10 rows, and explains that the alternate screen would erase the picker and choice from scrollback.
The output contract puts only the branch name plus newline on stdout, renders the UI to /dev/tty with stderr as fallback, and sends errors to stderr.
Says inline is the v2 default and to leave `v.AltScreen` unset; uses v2 APIs such as tea.KeyPressMsg and teatest/v2 and does not recommend v1-only options like WithAltScreen.
Git loading runs before p.Run(), so it stays out of Update, but results are not delivered through a tea.Cmd or message as the assertion requires.
Covers Update transition tests, golden View tests at pinned sizes (80×24, 60×24, 3 rows), and contract tests that stdout is exactly `name\n` with exit 130 on cancel and 2 on not-a-repo.
Says outright not to go full-screen and to use an inline picker capped like `fzf --height`, because the alt screen would hide the invoking command and leave nothing in scrollback.
The output contract puts only the branch name and a newline on stdout, with the UI on /dev/tty (stderr as fallback) and errors on stderr, and explains why this matters inside `$(...)`.
Says 'Inline, never `v.AltScreen`' using the v2 View field, and its other API references (tea.Interrupt, ErrInterrupted, teatest v2) are v2 rather than removed v1 options.

By default it runs git synchronously before the program starts; it only suggests moving the work into a tea.Cmd for repos with thousands of branches, so results do not normally come back through a Cmd or message.

Covers Update state-transition unit tests, golden frames at 80×24, 60×24 and the minimum size with a pinned color profile, and black-box binary tests that check stdout is exactly `name\n` and that cancel exits 130 and failures exit 1 or 2.
Opens with 'don't make it full-screen' and recommends height-capped inline mode, because the alternate screen would wipe the command and chosen branch from scrollback.
The output contract puts only the branch name plus newline on stdout, and all UI, the receipt and errors on stderr, falling back to /dev/tty, so $(...) captures only the value.
Says to leave v.AltScreen unset since inline is the v2 default, uses v2 APIs like tea.KeyPressMsg and v.Cursor, and recommends no removed v1 options.
All git loading happens before p.Run(), so it never runs in Update or blocks the event loop; it is not delivered via a tea.Cmd, but that alternative satisfies the same point.

Includes Update transition unit tests, golden frames at sizes including 40×8 with an ASCII color profile, and a PTY integration test asserting stdout is exactly the branch, Esc gives exit 130, and no TTY gives exit 2.
